items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: previously I'd been playing King Oliver, Lou Watter's sort of tunes.

ctx.x: Did your repertoire change when you went into this Melbourne New Orleans jazz band much?

Oh yes, yes, yes. Most of the tunes were new to me actually. They were based on, mainly on the records, Bunk Johnson, George Lewis and those men made, whereas previously I'd been playing King Oliver, Lou Watter's sort of tunes.
What were some of the typical ones you were playing before the Melbourne band?

items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: They stayed very much in the old, uh, mold of, uh, King Oliver Lou Bottas, sort of thing.

ctx.x: And this is in the forties mostly you're talking about?

Um, into the fifties too. Um. Um. No one, uh, took, uh, any great heed of the, um, Bunk Johnson, George Lewis, uh, type of band when it came out, um, until, um, 1957 when the Melbourne New Orleans Band, uh, started. Um. Um. They stayed very much in the old, uh, mold of, uh, King Oliver Lou Bottas, sort of thing.
Well, uh, back to Frank Johnson. Who was the star of that band? Was Johnson himself a star? I know.
